title: Leeman's letter after the first five-hour session
summary: Hinton introduces a taped note in which Leeman says the first session was exhausting but fruitful, and thanks the Smithsonian.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: This is a continuation of the Cliff Leeman

interview and recording. As Cliff will tell you on here, after a long session we had the other night, he went home and had some sort of chance to relax, and here he sort of explains himself and recollects. Here are some of his fine recollections -- and Cliff, thank you for this little note telling me what happened.

Dear friend Milt Hinton, this is Sunday, the 25th of February. Yesterday you interviewed me for the first time for my musical and personal history for five solid hours of tapes. It was like breaking the ice in Chesapeake Bay frozen over by the Coast Guard. I'm exhausted today.

We did accomplish so much, and I learned a lot from your interrogations as to the value of explaining names and places -- so they would be understood to those studying the tapes. You see, I drop names to you as a friend, who understands and I expect the uninitiated to understand, also, which they won't without further research on their part.
So, in the future interviews, I will be more explicit.

Just play that back for a balance, and found out I had a frog in my throat, upon commenting on the frozen over Chesapeake Bay and the ice should have been with a Coast Guard cutter. You must admit we worked pretty hard for our
first session, but it was so fruitful.

Before continuing with our work and thoughts at large, I want to say that I am greatly honored and deeply grateful to the Smithsonian Institute and those responsible for including me on their prestigous list of persons to be entered into the archives of jazz. I feel I have contributed much musically over a period of some 50 odd years that may be of importance to the uninformed and the interested -- student or researcher.
